anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: LXX φασεκ / phasek in the prophets-and-writings form Origen names.

choices.why: Technical: the Hebrew name was adapted into Greek sound.

pass_a_gloss: Since on this feast the people come out from Egypt, it is accordingly called phas, that is crossing. It not being possible for the name to be said in Hebrew through the Greek voice, Greeks being unable, because they cannot speak phas with the heavier Hebrew breathing, the name was Hellenized, and in the prophets phasek has been said, but more completely Hellenized it has been named pascha.
pass_b_english: For on this feast the people come out of Egypt, and so it is called phas, that is, crossing. The name cannot be spoken in Hebrew through the Greek tongue. The Greeks cannot say phas with the heavier breathing the Hebrews use. So the name was made Greek. In the prophets it is said phasek. When it has been more fully made Greek, it has been named pascha (Ezekiel 45:21) (2 Chronicles 35:1).
source_text: Ἐπεὶ [γ]ὰρ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ [ἑο]ρτῇ ὁ λαὸς ἐξ Α[ἰγύπτου] ἐξ[έρχε]ται, ἀκολούθως φ[ας] κα[λ]εῖ[ται, τοῦτ’ ἔσ]τιν διάβασ[ις]. Οὐχ οἷ[ον] τε οὖν ὄντος διὰ τῆς Ἑλλάδος φωνῆς [α]ὐτὸ ἑβραϊκῶς λ[έγεσ]θαι τὸ ὄνομα, [οὐ] δυναμ[ένων Ἑλ]λήνων π[α]ρὰ τὸ μὴ ἰ[σχύειν τ]ῇ δασείᾳ τ[ῇ] παρ’ Ἑβρα[ίοις] με[ί]ζονι λέγειν φας, ἐξηλ[λη]νίσθη τὸ ὄνομα, καὶ ἐν μ[ὲν τ]οῖς προφήταις φασὲκ [εἴ]ρηται, τελειοτέρω[ς] δὲ ἐξελληνισθὲν πάσχα ὠνόμασται.
